rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.2 and 3 <U+2013> the authors collected 210 soil cores at five depths in four seasons (autumn 2015 to spring 2017) in Qapqal County rice fields, measured ECe on saturation extracts, and built 3-D kriged salinity maps from their own data (Tables 1-3, Figures 3-7).
rows.notes: The study is a primary geostatistical mapping of seasonal soil salinity (ECe) in flood/surface-irrigated rice paddies in the Ili River Valley; it never tests, measures or mentions drip irrigation. It shows salt accumulation from spring to autumn under rice irrigation and dispersion from autumn to spring, with higher ECe in topsoil and deep subsoil and in poorly drained swales; it does not measure irrigation water quality or sodification (no SAR/ESP data) either. Hence no own evidence that salinization or sodification occurs under drip irrigation; the technology is mismatched.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study concerns surface-irrigated rice fields in cold semiarid Xinjiang, not drip systems; it reports seasonal ECe distribution via 3-D kriging with RMSE/R2 validation, Pearson correlations, and box plots, but no drip-related result.
